name: Anthropic Fellows paper: poisoning 1/200,000 of pretraining data can backdoor an agent to run attacker-chosen code, surviving SFT, DPO and RL
title: Anthropic Fellows paper: poisoning 1/200,000 of pretraining data can backdoor an agent to run attacker-chosen code, surviving SFT, DPO and RL
summary: A new Anthropic Fellows paper pretrains a Qwen3-4B-architecture model from scratch on a corpus with a tiny fraction of poisoned documents, then post-trains it with SFT, DPO and RL. Controlling about 1/200,000 of pretraining data was enough to make the resulting agent execute attacker-chosen code when it meets an ordinary file-path trigger, and the effect grew with model size.

appearances.title: Anthropic and others: poisoning 0.1% of pretraining data plants a remote-code-execution backdoor in a CLI agent
appearances.summary: Qwen3 models pretrained from scratch at 0.6B, 1.7B and 4B with 0.1% poisoned data, then post-trained cleanly into CLI agents. The backdoor survived SFT, DPO and tool-use RL and fired on about 92% of triggered prompts at 4B; the trigger can be an ordinary file path in the user's request. At 0.0005% poison (about 2,500 documents in 100B tokens) it still fired on 1.4% of prompts in one seed.
